post.summary: Type into a session: text, then named keys (enter, esc, tab, arrows, ctrl-c, ctrl-d, backspace), then Enter. Enter is pressed by default; pass draft=true (or submit=false) to type without sending. Takes either id: ses_… or the engine UUID. Read session_screen first and never send a blind Enter: at a menu it accepts whatever is highlighted (dismiss with esc). While a permission prompt shows, only a person's input is typed: an agent's is refused (403 person_required), except an oversight session's on a permission prompt. On a hibernated session it wakes first, and that wake is never forced: a session handed to a successor, or whose work item is already live in the same directory, is refused (409). Audited (byte count and keys, never the text).

merged_by.title: Merged By
merged_by.description: Who merged it, when the forge observation says.

ClaimPull.title: ClaimPull
ClaimPull.description: A pull request a completion claim was checked against (WI-1835).

source_instance_id.title: Source Instance Id
source_instance_id.description: The instance whose backup this instance was cloned from.

backup_taken_at.title: Backup Taken At
backup_taken_at.description: When the source's backup was taken: the copy's as-of time.

CloneInfo.title: CloneInfo
CloneInfo.description: That this instance is a copy of another one, and of when.

Comment.title: Comment
Comment.description:
A remark on a work item, attributed to an actor.

`kind` is `note` for an ordinary remark and `handoff` for the structured
hand-off a fresh session starts from (design C11). `handoff` is present
only on a hand-off comment.

kind.title: Kind
kind.description: `note` (default) is an ordinary remark. `handoff` is the structured hand-off a fresh session starts from, and requires `handoff`.

handoff.description: The structured fields of a hand-off: branch, head_sha, base, done, remaining, touch_points, gates_run, blockers, session. Required when kind is `handoff`, refused on a note.

write_back.title: Write Back
write_back.description: What happened upstream: skipped (the usual case), succeeded, or failed. A failure never fails the local write.

id.title: Id
id.description: Session id, in either form: Vogt's `ses_…` id or the engine's session UUID (`engine_session_id` in session.list; the only id an unlinked session has).

message.title: Message
message.description: The commit message. The repo's own git identity authors it.

paths.title: Paths
paths.description: Paths to stage before committing, relative to the repo. Empty commits whatever the worker already staged.

full_diff.title: Full Diff
full_diff.description: Return the full staged diff. Off by default, so the diff never enters a caller's context unasked; the digest and stat always do.

worktree.title: Worktree
worktree.description: Commit in this linked worktree instead of the session's own directory. It must be a worktree of the repo that directory belongs to; a stranger repo is refused. A worker's commit never lands in the repo's main checkout, where pool workers are launched: name the worker's own worktree (absolute or workspace-relative).

reason.title: Reason
reason.description: Why this write is being made (audited).

digest.title: Digest
digest.description: One line naming what was committed, e.g. the diff stat summary.

diff.title: Diff
diff.description: The full staged diff, only when full_diff was set.

review.title: Review
review.description: Hunks to read before trusting the commit: counts of dependency pins, `unsafe`, and foreign-function bindings.

age_seconds.title: Age Seconds
age_seconds.description: How old this answer is. Never refreshed implicitly.

adopted.title: Adopted
adopted.description: Whether this project opted into the contract. A project that has not is `not_applicable`, which is not a fault.

requires_install.title: Requires Install
requires_install.description: Whether the client needs Vogt's own code present. False for streamable HTTP, which is why it is the recommended path.

configuration.title: Configuration
configuration.description: Ready to use: JSON for a client config, or the document.

ConnectResult.title: ConnectResult
ConnectResult.description:
The connection facts, and the client configuration built from them.

`url` is `None` when nobody has configured one. That is deliberately not
a guess: a URL the server invented would be wrong in exactly the
deployment this field exists for, and a client cannot tell a wrong URL
from an unreachable one.

ConnectionInfo.title: ConnectionInfo
ConnectionInfo.description:
What a client needs to connect, from the server itself (DEPLOY §4.3).

One generated document rather than per-client hand-copied config: the
`:18081` incident began as a URL that lived in seven places and was
retired in one.

ContractAdoptParams.title: ContractAdoptParams
ContractAdoptParams.description: Opt a registered project into the contract.

status.title: Status
status.description: What compliance reports for this project after the change.

project.title: Project
project.description: A registered project slug. Records the result with its age.

ContractCheckParams.title: ContractCheckParams
ContractCheckParams.description: Evaluate a registered project and record the result.

criteria.title: Criteria
criteria.description: Every rule evaluated — not only the failures.

inapplicable.title: Inapplicable
inapplicable.description: Criteria declared unmeetable here, with their reasons.

recommendations.title: Recommendations
recommendations.description: What would close each failing criterion.

detail.title: Detail
detail.description: Why this answer is the answer, where the status alone would not say: a project that has not adopted the contract, or a root path that could not be read.

path.title: Path
path.description: Any folder or repository, registered or not. Stores nothing.

ContractEvaluateParams.title: ContractEvaluateParams
ContractEvaluateParams.description:
A dry run against any path. Reads, stores nothing, needs no reason.

Split from `ContractCheckParams` because the two are different
operations wearing one name. This one changes nothing, so the audit has
nothing to record — and demanding a reason for it meant the CLI collected a
justification for a write that never happened, then discarded it. It also
forced `project.write` scope on a read, so a read-only token could not
evaluate a contract against a folder at all.

declared.title: Declared
declared.description: True when the criterion is now inapplicable here.

rule.title: Rule
rule.description: The criterion's rule, as an evaluation reports it: `required_file` or `required_dir`.

target.title: Target
target.description: The criterion's target, as an evaluation reports it: `LICENSE`, `src`, `design`.

ContractInapplicableParams.title: ContractInapplicableParams
ContractInapplicableParams.description: Declare that a criterion cannot apply to a project.

projects.title: Projects
projects.description: How many projects this collector has ever swept. Cumulative, which is what the operation's name promises; it used to be the scope of the most recent sweep, so a `--project`-scoped run made every collector look as though it had only ever seen one.

registered.title: Registered
registered.description: The denominator: projects registered on this instance.

last_sweep_scope.title: Last Sweep Scope
last_sweep_scope.description: How many projects the most recent sweep was asked about. Reported separately so a scoped sweep and a collector that failed on seven of eight projects stop looking alike.

never_swept.title: Never Swept
never_swept.description: Registered projects this collector has never looked at. The number a reader is usually after, and the one that used to have to be inferred from a count that could not support it.

unswept_project_ids.title: Unswept Project Ids
unswept_project_ids.description: Registered projects no collector has ever swept. A registered project nothing has looked at has no evidence behind anything it claims, and is the case the not-collected rule exists to keep visible.

identity_ref.title: Identity Ref
identity_ref.description: Stable identity, e.g. agent:claude-code or local:sprooty.

name.title: Name
name.description: Display name; the slug is derived from it.

root_path.title: Root Path
root_path.description: Directory to scaffold into. Created if absent; existing files are never overwritten.

owner.title: Owner
owner.description: Recorded in the scaffold. Defaults to the acting principal.

reason.title: Reason
reason.description: Why this write is being made (audited).

created_paths.title: Created Paths
created_paths.description: Files and directories written. Existing ones are left alone.

skipped_paths.title: Skipped Paths
skipped_paths.description: Contract paths that already existed and were not touched.

actor.title: Actor
actor.description: An existing human actor's identity_ref to attach the login to. Omitted, a new actor human:<username> is created.

scopes.title: Scopes
scopes.description: Comma-separated scopes every session this user logs in to holds.

session.title: Session
session.description: The session to wake (ses_… or engine UUID). Default: your own session, from your token.

note.title: Note
note.description: Appended to the wake message, e.g. what to do next.

ttl_seconds.title: Ttl Seconds
ttl_seconds.description: How long the watch stays armed: default 24 h, at most 14 d. Past it the watch reads `expired` and wakes nobody.

reason.title: Reason
reason.description: Why this write is being made (audited).

CreateWatchParams.title: CreateWatchParams
CreateWatchParams.description: Arm a watch: wake a session with the outcome when the trigger fires.

local_only.title: Local Only
local_only.description: Create the item locally without writing it upstream. On a linked project a create normally goes through to the forge, and a write-back policy that does not permit 'create' refuses it; pass this to opt in to a native, local-only item instead — it carries no upstream subject yet and is exactly what a later `forge link` or `forge writeback` migrates upstream. Default off: the refusal stays the default so nothing is created locally by surprise.

applicable.title: Applicable
applicable.description: Whether this criterion can apply to this project at all . False is a declaration somebody made and gave a reason for — a Cargo workspace has no root `src/` — and an inapplicable criterion is reported but never counted as failing.

tracked.title: Tracked
tracked.description: Whether the repository carries this. Null where it could not be asked — an unregistered path, or a directory that is not a checkout. False alongside a file that exists on disk is the present-but-untracked case: no clone would have it.

id.title: Id
id.description: The grant id (grt_…).

reason.title: Reason
reason.description: Why this write is being made (audited).

asker_session.title: Asker Session
asker_session.description: The asker's engine session id, if a session.

state.title: State
state.description: `expired` is a pending decision past `expires_at`; it implies no answer.

DecisionView.title: DecisionView
DecisionView.description: A decision as callers read it.

DepRef.title: DepRef
DepRef.description:
One reference from a project to another project.

Records *which projects reference which*, by filesystem path or
repository URL, and stops there: no lockfile is parsed and no package
version is resolved (r2 decision, ARCHITECTURE.md).

DependencySummary.title: DependencySummary
DependencySummary.description: What this project references, and what references it.

work_items.title: Work Items
work_items.description: Work item refs the commit subject names.

DeployedCommit.title: DeployedCommit
DeployedCommit.description: A commit on the lane's branch that the lane is not running yet.

lane.title: Lane
lane.description: The same name; kept for existing readers.

status.title: Status
status.description: at_head: deployed revision is the branch head; behind: commits on the branch are not deployed; diverged: the deployed revision is not on the branch; unknown: the evidence could not say (see detail); not_collected: no sweep has read this lane.

deployed_from.title: Deployed From
deployed_from.description: Where deployed_sha came from: the running instance's version endpoint (live) or the deploy pipeline's receipt.

source_tag.title: Source Tag
source_tag.description: The tag the receipt says was deployed.

truncated.title: Truncated
truncated.description: More commits are behind than are listed (commits_behind is still exact).

DeployedLaneView.title: DeployedLaneView
DeployedLaneView.description: One lane: what it runs, and how far that is behind its branch.

configured.title: Configured
configured.description: How many lanes `deploy_lanes` configures in total.

DeployedVersionsResult.title: DeployedVersionsResult
DeployedVersionsResult.description: Every configured lane, honest about lanes nobody has read yet.

mirrors.title: Mirrors
mirrors.description: Copies this project carries of other projects' source.

mirrored_by.title: Mirrored By
mirrored_by.description: Projects carrying a copy of this project's source.

status.title: Status
status.description: Whether the dependency collector has walked this project. `not_collected` makes the counts above meaningless rather than informative: nothing was read, so nothing was found.

manifests_read.title: Manifests Read
manifests_read.description: How many manifests the last walk actually parsed.

unsupported_manifests.title: Unsupported Manifests
unsupported_manifests.description: Manifests present in a format the collector does not read (`go.mod`, `pom.xml`, …). A project whose graph lives entirely in one of these reports no references and has plenty.

unreadable_manifests.title: Unreadable Manifests
unreadable_manifests.description: Manifests in a supported format that would not parse.

DepsResult.title: DepsResult
DepsResult.description:
The dependency graph around one project.

Carries `freshness` because a graph is an aggregate over sweeps, and an
empty graph with no sweep behind it means "not collected", not "this
project depends on nothing". `status` narrows the same
point to this project: estate-wide freshness cannot say whether the
dependency collector has ever walked *this* tree.

DiagnosticCheck.title: DiagnosticCheck
DiagnosticCheck.description: One readiness check, named, with what it found.

status.title: Status
status.description: The worst of `checks`; not_configured checks do not count.

image_digest.title: Image Digest
image_digest.description: As the deployment stated it (`image_digest`); null if unstated.

DiagnosticsResult.title: DiagnosticsResult
DiagnosticsResult.description: Is this instance what it should be, and is it well — in one read.

auto_accept.title: Auto Accept
auto_accept.description: Apply the shipped low-risk policy: state-sync kinds are accepted automatically, destructive or structural ones never are.

already_open.title: Already Open
already_open.description: Findings that already had an open proposal, so were not re-raised.

superseded.title: Superseded
superseded.description: Open proposals this run marked as raised under evidence a later sweep no longer reproduces. They are still open and still need a person; the flag only tells the inbox which ones are worth reading first.

not_collected.title: Not Collected
not_collected.description: Registered projects no collector has ever swept. Nothing could be raised for them, which is a different answer from finding no drift there.

human_gated.title: Human Gated
human_gated.description: Kinds the default policy never auto-accepts, and why.

DriftListResult.title: DriftListResult
DriftListResult.description:
The drift inbox.

`freshness` is load-bearing here rather than decorative: an empty inbox
is reassuring only if something has looked recently. Without it, a
collector that stopped running reads as "no drift".

DriftProposal.title: DriftProposal
DriftProposal.description: A machine-raised question, resolved by a human or an agent.

overrides.title: Overrides
overrides.description: Where the task contradicted this policy, one line per axis (PR vs push only, merge, base branch, deploy). The policy wins and the brief says so; empty when the task agreed or set none.

EffectivePolicy.title: EffectivePolicy
EffectivePolicy.description: The landing rule a started session runs under (WI-1832).

EngineAgentTaskStatus.title: EngineAgentTaskStatus
EngineAgentTaskStatus.description: The engine's scheduled agent tasks and the prompt files they left.

EngineDiskStatus.title: EngineDiskStatus
EngineDiskStatus.description: The workspace volume's usage, as the engine reports it (WI-1304).

EngineHistoryStatus.title: EngineHistoryStatus
EngineHistoryStatus.description: The engine's session-history archive, when it keeps one.

EngineLag.title: EngineLag
EngineLag.description: How often one event subscriber fell behind, and by how much.

engine_session_id.title: Engine Session Id
engine_session_id.description: The engine's id (UUID) for the session the token is for.

revoke.title: Revoke
revoke.description: Revoke the session's tokens instead of minting one.

reason.title: Reason
reason.description: Why this write is being made (audited).

engine.title: Engine
engine.description: Why the engine could not be asked; null when it answered.

auto_agent_auth.title: Auto Agent Auth
auto_agent_auth.description: Whether the engine resolves agent credentials at launch.

workspace_root.title: Workspace Root
workspace_root.description: The root every session and file path is under.

event_lag.title: Event Lag
event_lag.description: Event subscribers that fell behind since the engine started, by name. Empty is healthy.

disk.description: The workspace volume. needs_attention once used space passes the engine's threshold (85% by default).

EngineStatusResult.title: EngineStatusResult
EngineStatusResult.description:
The session engine's operational report, as the GUI's Settings shows it.

`engine` is set, and the rest left at its defaults, when the engine is not
configured or could not be asked: an outage is said, never rendered as an
idle engine.

Event.title: Event
Event.description:
One row of the ordered notification feed.

`seq` is the `/events` cursor — a single monotonic sequence over a single
table, so no client ever merges orderings across the two stores.

project.title: Project
project.description: Export one project (by slug): its work items with their comments and relations, and only the initiatives, labels and actors they reference. Omitted, the whole instance is exported.

export_format_version.title: Export Format Version
export_format_version.description: The file's format. 2 carries what an applying import needs.

host.title: Host
host.description: The configured forge host to link, for example github.com or a Forgejo host named under forge_token_files.

token.title: Token
token.description: The Personal Access Token. Validated, then stored encrypted at rest under `forge_account_key_file` and never returned by any surface. To revoke it, unlink here and revoke it upstream too.

reason.title: Reason
reason.description: Why this write is being made (audited).

ForgeAccountLinkParams.title: ForgeAccountLinkParams
ForgeAccountLinkParams.description:
Link the acting actor's own forge account by pasting a PAT.

The token is validated against the forge, then stored encrypted at rest
and never echoed. Linking arms upstream writes attributed to *you*: the
scope of what those writes can do is the scope of the token you paste.

login.title: Login
login.description: The linked login; null once unlinked.

ForgeAccountResult.title: ForgeAccountResult
ForgeAccountResult.description: The outcome of a link or unlink — status only, never the token.

host.title: Host
host.description: The forge host to unlink. Deletes the stored token.

reason.title: Reason
reason.description: Why this write is being made (audited).

scopes.title: Scopes
scopes.description: The token's granted scopes as the forge reports them (`X-OAuth-Scopes`), or empty when the forge did not say.

ForgeAccountView.title: ForgeAccountView
ForgeAccountView.description: One linked account, never carrying the token.

owner.title: Owner
owner.description: Repository owner, as `forge repos` lists it.

name.title: Name
name.description: Repository name, as `forge repos` lists it.

host.title: Host
host.description: The configured forge host, for example github.com or a Forgejo host named under forge_token_files.

display_name.title: Display Name
display_name.description: Project display name. Defaults to the repository name.

root_path.title: Root Path
root_path.description: Where to clone to. Defaults to `<import_root>/<slug>`; supply this only when the repository must live somewhere specific.

consolidate.title: Consolidate
consolidate.description: Read existing issues, PRs, labels and releases after registering . Read-only, and on by default so the imported project arrives as upstream-truth rather than looking empty.

reason.title: Reason
reason.description: Why this write is being made (audited).

ForgeImportParams.title: ForgeImportParams
ForgeImportParams.description:
Import a repository the picker listed, as a project.

Named exactly as `forge.repos` shows it — `owner` and `name` — because
this is the verb that turns one of those listed rows into a project:
clone under the acting credential, register, and consolidate. The
credential that reaches the repository to list it is the credential the
clone runs under, so a private repository a personal PAT can see imports
without the instance file token ever needing access to it.

ForgeLinkParams.title: ForgeLinkParams
ForgeLinkParams.description:
Make a registered project upstream-truth.

Validated, not assumed: the project must carry a `repo_url` a registered
provider matches and a usable credential (the acting actor's linked PAT,
or the instance file token). A missing precondition is a typed
refusal that names it.

ForgeLinkResult.title: ForgeLinkResult
ForgeLinkResult.description:
`forge.link`'s receipt: the linked project, and what migrated.

`migrated` lists every open native item published upstream and re-keyed
during this link, oldest first. A mid-migration provider failure raises
instead — naming which items migrated and which are still native — so a
result in hand means every listed item, and only those, moved.

name.title: Name
name.description: Repository name to create; defaults to the project slug.

private.title: Private
private.description: Whether the new repository is private. Private by default: publishing makes a repository, not an announcement.

ForgePublishParams.title: ForgePublishParams
ForgePublishParams.description:
Create the remote and make the project upstream-truth.

The first verb that creates upstream state and pushes commits, which is
why every precondition is typed and checked up front: not already
linked, no `repo_url` to clobber, a clean checkout on a named branch,
and a usable credential. The push is plain — never forced.

branch.title: Branch
branch.description: The local branch pushed as the default.

revision.title: Revision
revision.description: The commit the push left as the remote head.

ForgePublishResult.title: ForgePublishResult
ForgePublishResult.description: What `forge.publish` did, in the order it did it.

visibility.title: Visibility
visibility.description: 'public' or 'private', as the forge reports it.

url.title: Url
url.description: The repository's web URL; what an import is driven with.

already_registered.title: Already Registered
already_registered.description: Whether this instance already has a project whose repository URL is this repo — computed against the declared project list, so a select-all can skip what is already imported.

ForgeRepoView.title: ForgeRepoView
ForgeRepoView.description: One repository the credential can see, as the picker shows it.

login.title: Login
login.description: Whose credential enumerated these — the linked actor login, or null when the instance file token was used.

detail.title: Detail
detail.description: Why the list is empty when it is — no forge configured for the host, for instance — so an empty picker reads as 'not collected' rather than 'you have no repositories'.

collectors.title: Collectors
collectors.description: Per collector: how long ago it last completed.

Freshness.title: Freshness
Freshness.description:
How old the evidence behind an answer is.

Every aggregating answer carries one. `oldest_relevant_sweep` is the
honest number: an answer is exactly as fresh as the least fresh thing it
depends on.

GitStoryDriftView.title: GitStoryDriftView
GitStoryDriftView.description:
One contradiction between a work item and its git evidence.

Derived and read-only: Vogt *reports* the disagreement — a closed
item with an open PR, a merged PR under an open item, an active branch on a
done item — it does not reconcile it. `provenance` says which observation
the contradiction was read from, so a reader can check it.

HandoffFields.title: HandoffFields
HandoffFields.description:
The structured half of a hand-off comment (design C11).

Every field is optional: a hand-off records what the writer knows, and a
field left out means "not stated", not "empty on purpose". Free text stays
on the comment body.

id.title: Id
id.description: Session id, in either form: Vogt's `ses_…` id or the engine's session UUID (`engine_session_id` in session.list; the only id an unlinked session has).

allow_shell.title: Allow Shell
allow_shell.description: Hibernate a session that has no agent conversation to resume (a shell). It wakes as a fresh process in the same directory.

superseded_by.title: Superseded By
superseded_by.description: The session taking over this one's work (ses_… or the engine UUID). Recorded on the hibernation, and a later wake is refused unless forced — so the work stays with one session.

wake_on.description: Arm a watch before hibernating: the session is woken, and told the outcome, when this trigger fires (see watch_create).

wake_on_ttl_seconds.title: Wake On Ttl Seconds
wake_on_ttl_seconds.description: How long the watch stays armed: default 24 h, at most 14 d. Past it the watch reads `expired` and wakes nobody.

cold_wake_opt_out.title: Cold Wake Opt Out
cold_wake_opt_out.description: Never compact this session on a cold wake (WI-2037): a wake always resumes its full transcript, even when the deployment's cold_wake_compaction is on and the prompt cache has expired. Unset keeps the session's current choice (a new session follows the deployment).

reason.title: Reason
reason.description: Why this write is being made (audited).

engine.title: Engine
engine.description: What the engine said, when it could not be asked. Empty history is returned rather than an error, so an outage never reads as 'no history' .

live.title: Live
live.description: True when the match is in a running session's live output.

HistoryOutputMatch.title: HistoryOutputMatch
HistoryOutputMatch.description:
One hit from a session-output search.

`live` distinguishes a match in a running session's scrollback from one in
the archived index. The snippet is plain text — terminal output is
untrusted and is never marked up.

template.title: Template
template.description: The session template it was started from.

role.title: Role
role.description: `worker` or `oversight`, as last set; null on older rows.

conversation_agent.title: Conversation Agent
conversation_agent.description: The agent CLI of the last conversation the session ran — one the engine launched, or one typed into its shell that reported itself.

conversation_id.title: Conversation Id
conversation_id.description: That conversation's id. Kept after it ends, so a lost session can be resumed: session_start(template=resume_template, resume=conversation_id, role=role).

work_item.title: Work Item
work_item.description: The work item the session served when it ended, as last bound (session.bind_work); null when it was bound to none. Resume binds it again: session_start(..., resume=conversation_id) then session_bind_work(work_item).

resume_template.title: Resume Template
resume_template.description: The template that resumes conversation_id here, worked out against the engine's templates now; null when nothing can resume it.

HistorySessionRow.title: HistorySessionRow
HistorySessionRow.description:
One row of the engine's archived-session listing.

A live session the engine chooses to include carries a null `ended_at`
and `exit_code`, exactly as it appears in the GUI history list.

repo.title: Repo
repo.description: Repository to import: `owner/name`, `host/owner/name`, or an HTTPS/SSH repository URL for GitHub or a configured Forgejo host.

name.title: Name
name.description: Display name. Defaults to the repository's own name.

root_path.title: Root Path
root_path.description: Where to clone to. Defaults to `<import_root>/<slug>`; supply this only when one repository must live somewhere specific.

consolidate.title: Consolidate
consolidate.description: Read existing issues, PRs, labels and releases after registering. Read-only, and on by default because a project that arrives empty looks like a project with no work.

reason.title: Reason
reason.description: Why this write is being made (audited).

ImportProjectParams.title: ImportProjectParams
ImportProjectParams.description:
Bring a repository that lives on a configured forge into Vogt.

`repo` is named by the caller and is never chosen from a list: there is
no listing operation, and adding one would be the registration-candidate
listing that was deliberately removed.

remote.title: Remote
remote.description: The remote that was cloned, without credentials.

revision.title: Revision
revision.description: HEAD at the moment of import.

cloned.title: Cloned
cloned.description: False when the destination already held a clone of the same remote and was registered as it stood.

consolidated.description: What the read-only consolidation found, if it ran.

InboxAction.title: InboxAction
InboxAction.description: A typed target for the action a row can take.

InboxCoverage.title: InboxCoverage
InboxCoverage.description: Coverage and count for one normalized source.

actor_login.title: Actor Login
actor_login.description: Who caused this occurrence, where the forge said so.

actor_kind.title: Actor Kind
actor_kind.description: human or bot; null when no author could be resolved. Drift, CI and agent entries are the instance itself: bot.

actor_relation.title: Actor Relation
actor_relation.description: org_member: on the repository's owning org's member list (or reported MEMBER/OWNER). external: a person outside the org, outside collaborators included. unknown: not resolvable.

InboxEntry.title: InboxEntry
InboxEntry.description: One server-normalized occurrence in the attention stream.

actor_unknown_hidden.title: Actor Unknown Hidden
actor_unknown_hidden.description: With actor=external: how many entries matching every other filter were hidden because their author is unknown.

InboxSavedFilter.title: InboxSavedFilter
InboxSavedFilter.description:
The structured Inbox filter a person saves (`inbox.filter`).

Search text is deliberately absent: it is a temporary, client-side narrowing
of what is on screen, and the sidebar badge never counts by it.

Initiative.title: Initiative
Initiative.description: A cross-project epic, carrying weight that feeds ranking.

close_proposed.title: Close Proposed
close_proposed.description: Whether closing the initiative proposed closing this tracking issue (never an automatic upstream close).

InitiativeTrackingIssue.title: InitiativeTrackingIssue
InitiativeTrackingIssue.description: One repo's tracking issue, after a publish.

display_name.title: Display Name
display_name.description: The first operator's name, e.g. 'Ada Lovelace'.

NotificationsResult.description:
The inbox, and what it is honestly able to be.

supported.title: Supported

writable_reason.description: Why `writable` is what it is, naming the way forward.

PublishInitiativeParams.title: PublishInitiativeParams
PublishInitiativeParams.description:
Project an initiative onto a forge tracking issue per linked repo.

Additive and forward-only: for each forge-linked project the initiative
spans, Vogt creates or adopts one tracking issue labelled
``initiative:<slug>`` and re-renders its managed task list. Nothing is ever
closed or deleted — a closed initiative *proposes* its tracking issues be
closed (drift), it never writes the close.

PublishInitiativeResult.title: PublishInitiativeResult
PublishInitiativeResult.description: What `initiative.publish` did, one row per repo the initiative spans.

classified.title: Classified
classified.description: Whether anything actually said what kind of work this is. False means `kind` is this product's guess from an absence of signal — an unlabelled forge issue — and that the subject may be missing from the view a reader expected to find it in. Declared work is always classified: somebody typed the kind in.

ref.title: Ref
ref.description: `WI-7` for declared work, or the observed subject key.

adopted_as.title: Adopted As
adopted_as.description: Work item reference, when this subject has been adopted.

RankedItem.title: RankedItem
RankedItem.description:
One entry of a ranked view — declared or observed.

Observed-first means both halves appear in the same list, ordered by the
same weights. The common fields are what ranking needs and what a
reader wants; `item` carries the whole work item when there is one, and
`subject_key` points at the evidence when there is not.

Readiness.title: Readiness
Readiness.description:
Ready means the stores are migrated *to this build's schema* and
answering.

Readiness gates traffic until migration completes (`DEPLOYMENT.md`),
which is why this reports schema versions rather
than a bare boolean: a red probe should say what is wrong.

**Both numbers are reported per store, and that is the whole of the fix
made at r13.** Until then this answered with the *applied* version alone
and said `ready` whenever the stores responded — a fact about the disk
that answers no question a deployer has. An image whose migration had not
run looked exactly like one whose migration had, so a container carrying
a new migration came up green and failed afterwards on a missing table,
as a SQL error at whatever touched it first rather than as a red probe.
Comparing the two is what turns that into an outage the orchestrator can
see before it routes traffic.

capturing.title: Capturing

RecommendationView.title: RecommendationView

Advisory output. A `scaffold` remedy is one `project scaffold`
performs; a `judgement` remedy is an instruction addressed to an actor —
readable by a person, executable by an agent, applied implicitly by
neither. Nothing may treat any of it as authority.

One line of session state (design C1).

session, and null until then. `supervisor` is named for WI-956 and stays

SessionDigestResult.title: SessionDigestResult
SessionDigestResult.description:
What an overseer reads instead of screen, last reply and git log (C3).

One engine `get_session`. Numbers come from that row's `economics` when
the engine sends one, and are null when it does not — this read does not
meter a transcript and does not open a transcript file. `last_reply_excerpt`
is likewise only what the row already carries, clipped to 120 characters.
`context_pct` needs the caller to name `context_window`. `budget_line` is
the same line `session.economics` builds, from those numbers.

SessionEconomicsResult.title: SessionEconomicsResult
SessionEconomicsResult.description:
What a session's agent transcript cost (C16).

Read from the same transcript `session.last_reply` finds, whole rather
than tailed. `context_tokens` is the latest turn's window, not a sum.
`usage_measured` is true only when that number came from recorded usage
(Claude Code); Klaudia and Codex are estimated at four characters per
token. `cost_usd` stays null: this product has no price table, and a zero
would say the session was free. `commits` and `files_changed` stay null
until a worktree is measured; zero would say the tree was clean.
`detail` set means the transcript could not be read, and the counts are
then the empty reading, not a claim that the session did nothing.

SessionLastReplyResult.description:
The last assistant messages of the agent conversation a session runs.

Read from the agent's own transcript (Claude Code or Codex JSONL), so a
reply is whole and current — not cut at the screen's edge or mangled by
redraws. `basis` says how the conversation was found: `session-id` /
`resume-id` (named on the command line), `engine-id` (a Claude Code
session the engine started), or `cwd` (the newest transcript in the
session's directory since it started — a guess when two agents share a
directory). Empty `messages` with `detail` set means it could not be read.

engine.title: Engine
engine.description: What the engine said, when it could not be asked. The links are still returned: Vogt's record of what it started does not depend on the engine being up.

total.title: Total
total.description: How many sessions match the filters, before `limit`/`offset`. `truncated` is set when this page is not all of them. When more declared links match than `session.list` reads (500), `total` is one past the number actually read and `truncated` stays true on every page, including an empty one past the end.

truncated.description: More sessions match than this page returns.

hidden_count.title: Hidden Count
hidden_count.description: How many sessions the engine left out of its default list (WI-1289), counted before this operation's own filters and paging. 0 from an engine that does not report it. Those sessions are in `sessions` only when `include_hidden` was set.

id.title: Id
id.description: The reporting session, in either id form. Omit it from inside a session Vogt started (its token names the session).

summary.title: Summary

A session's own typed report (WI-2039): what it says it did or needs.

Posted with `session.report`. Every field is the reporting agent's text:
untrusted data, never instructions. A structured field left null was not

The agent, model and effort a session is running, each with where

ready.title: Ready
ready.description: The engine's view of whether the session awaits input. False while awaiting-approval: answer the dialog, do not type at it.

scrollback.title: Scrollback
scrollback.description: Lines above the screen, oldest first, when asked for.

SessionScreenResult.title: SessionScreenResult
SessionScreenResult.description:
The terminal's current visible screen, as rendered text.

What a person looking at the terminal would see right now — not the
output log (`session.log_tail`). Terminal content is untrusted data.

linked.title: Linked
linked.description: True when Vogt declared this session; false for one the engine holds but Vogt never linked (project/work_item/actor/reason null).

work_item.title: Work Item
work_item.description: The work item the session serves, e.g. WI-7: set at session.start or re-declared by session.bind_work. For an unlinked session, the engine's `work_item` label, when one was bound.

work_item_title.title: Work Item Title
work_item_title.description: That work item's title, joined at read time.

work_item_state.title: Work Item State
work_item_state.description: That work item's workflow state, joined at read time — a bound session on a `done` item is still allowed, and shown muted.

actor.title: Actor
actor.description: Actor the session's writes are attributed to. Null for an unlinked engine session, which declares no actor.

model.title: Model
model.description: The model this session was started with. What was asked for, not what the agent is using now.

effort.title: Effort
effort.description: The reasoning effort it was started with.

reason.title: Reason
reason.description: Why Vogt started the session. Null for an unlinked engine session, which declares no reason.

purpose.title: Purpose
purpose.description: The dispatch purpose the start named (WI-1323): implement, implement-careful, review, mechanical, investigate or design. Null when it named none, and for an unlinked engine session.

started_by_session.title: Started By Session
started_by_session.description: Engine id of the session that started this one (WI-1323), read from the starter's verified identity. Null for a person's start.

started_by_kind.title: Started By Kind
started_by_kind.description: Who started it (WI-1323): `person`, or the starting session's engine role at that moment. Null when the engine could not be asked, and for a session started before this was recorded.

started_at.title: Started At
started_at.description: When the session started: Vogt's record for a linked session, the engine's creation time for an unlinked one, null only when neither is known.

name.title: Name
name.description: Live from the engine: the session's display name, as the GUI shows it (session.rename changes it). None when the engine could not be asked.

command.title: Command
command.description: Live from the engine: the command the session runs.

exit_code.title: Exit Code
exit_code.description: Live from the engine: the process's exit code once it has ended; null while it runs.

activity_changed_at.title: Activity Changed At
activity_changed_at.description: Live from the engine: when `activity` last changed.

conversation_agent.title: Conversation Agent
conversation_agent.description: Live from the engine: the agent CLI whose conversation the session runs (with `conversation_id`), when known.

activity.title: Activity
activity.description: Live from the engine: idle / running / waiting-for-input / awaiting-approval (an agent CLI's permission dialog; see `approval`) while the process runs; exited (exit code 0) / errored (any other code) once it has ended. None when the engine could not be asked.

alive.title: Alive
alive.description: Whether the session's process is still running on the engine: false once it has exited or the engine no longer has it. None if the engine could not be asked.

turn_started_at.title: Turn Started At
turn_started_at.description: Live from the engine: when the current (or last) turn began — the last time the session went running from idle or waiting. With `last_output_at` it tells a long turn from a hung one.

last_output_at.title: Last Output At
last_output_at.description: Live from the engine: when the terminal last printed anything.

done_at.title: Done At
done_at.description: Live from the engine: when an autopilot session declared itself done (`AUTOPILOT: DONE`) this turn. Cleared when the next turn starts; null otherwise.

approval.description: The permission dialog on screen while activity is awaiting-approval; null otherwise.

blocked.description: The agent's own report that it is blocked on a person (session.report_blocked); null when it is not. Do not re-prompt a blocked session: do what it asks, or answer it.

last_reply_excerpt.title: Last Reply Excerpt
last_reply_excerpt.description: The first ~300 characters of the session's agent's latest reply, redacted, from its own transcript (session.list only, live agent sessions whose conversation id is known). Null for a shell, or when no transcript is found. session.last_reply has the whole message.

latest_report.description: The session's newest `session.report` (WI-2039): its own typed account of progress, result, question or blocker. Prefer it over `last_reply_excerpt`; null when it never reported.

hibernation.description: Set while the session is hibernated (activity `hibernated`): its processes were stopped to free memory and it is kept to be woken by resuming its conversation (session.wake, or session.input, which wakes it). Null otherwise.

keep_awake.title: Keep Awake
keep_awake.description: Pinned awake (session.keep_awake): never hibernated by policy. None when the engine could not be asked.

autopilot.title: Autopilot
autopilot.description: On autopilot (WI-949): the engine re-prompts it when it stops with work left and its idle policy leaves it awake. Turns false once the agent prints `AUTOPILOT: DONE` or the engine's nudge cap is reached. None when the engine could not be asked.

autopilot_nudges.title: Autopilot Nudges
autopilot_nudges.description: How many times the engine has told it to carry on.

role.title: Role
role.description: What the session is for (session.set_role): `oversight` for one nominated to supervise other sessions, `worker` otherwise. None when the engine could not be asked.

stopped_by.title: Stopped By
stopped_by.description: Live from the engine: who asked the session to stop, when it was stopped on request (activity `stopped`).

stop_reason.title: Stop Reason
stop_reason.description: Live from the engine: why it was stopped.

permission_mode.title: Permission Mode
permission_mode.description: Live from the engine: the permission posture when it is not the default — `accept-edits`, or `bypass` (no permission checks). Null is the default posture.

posture_lost_on_resume.title: Posture Lost On Resume
posture_lost_on_resume.description: Live from the engine: the session showed bypass before it was hibernated and was woken without it (WI-2252). A wake replays only the posture a person gave at the start, so a bypass granted later (Shift+Tab, a hand-typed flag) is lost; a person re-grants it in the session's terminal.

account.title: Account
account.description: Live from the engine: the named Claude Code account the session runs under. Null is the engine's default account.

running.description: The agent, model and reasoning effort the session is actually running, resolved from its transcript, its command line, or what it was started with — `model`/`effort` above are only what was asked. Live and hibernated sessions.

resources.description: Live from the engine: RSS, CPU and process count of the session's process tree, sampled every few seconds. Null before the first sample, for a hibernated or exited session, or when the engine cannot sample.

budget.description: Live from the engine: the limits this session was started with (C7). Null when it has none, or when the engine could not be asked.

conversation_id.title: Conversation Id
conversation_id.description: The agent CLI's own id for the conversation this session runs, when the engine knows it — what a wake resumes, and what session.start's `resume` takes.

SessionSummary.title: SessionSummary
SessionSummary.description:
One session, as Vogt knows it and as the engine currently reports it.

Two halves on purpose. `id`, `project`, `work_item` and `reason` are
Vogt's declared link — written once, audited, and true whatever the
engine is doing. `activity` and `alive` are read from the engine at the
moment of asking and are never stored: a cached activity state would be
a claim about a running process, which is the one thing this product
refuses to invent.

A session the engine holds but Vogt never linked is reported too, so the
surface answers "what is running here", not only "what did Vogt start".
Such a session has no declared half: `linked` is false, and `project`,
`work_item`, `actor` and `reason` are null because there is nothing
audited to name. `id` and `engine_session_id` then carry the engine's id
(the only handle there is), and `started_at` is the engine's own creation
time — never a fabricated one.

counts.title: Counts
counts.description: Rows per attention class, plus `needs_you` and `total`.

engine.title: Engine
engine.description: Why the engine could not be asked, when it could not.

SessionSweepResult.title: SessionSweepResult
SessionSweepResult.description: Every live and hibernated session at once, most urgent first.

attention.title: Attention
attention.description: approval (a permission dialog, startup gate or question menu) / blocked / waiting (at its prompt, wants the next instruction) / stalled (running, silent too long) / running / idle / hibernated / exited / unknown. The table is ordered by it.

screen_tail.title: Screen Tail
screen_tail.description: The last non-blank lines of its screen. Untrusted terminal text.

blocked_since.title: Blocked Since
blocked_since.description: When the session's blocked report was made, if it has one.

blocked_age_s.title: Blocked Age S
blocked_age_s.description: How old the blocked report is, in seconds.

blocked_stale.title: Blocked Stale
blocked_stale.description: The blocked report predates the session's current turn: it went back to work after reporting, so the report no longer says what it waits on and the row is not counted in `needs_you` (WI-1834).

claim_check.description: On a `done` row bound to a work item: its AUTOPILOT: DONE claim checked against git and the forge (WI-1835).

SessionSweepRow.title: SessionSweepRow
SessionSweepRow.description: One session in the oversight table.

next_cursor.title: Next Cursor
next_cursor.description: The seq to pass as `cursor` on the next wait.

SessionWaitAnyResult.title: SessionWaitAnyResult
SessionWaitAnyResult.description: Why a wait across sessions ended.

id.title: Id
id.description: The id the caller named, as given.

outcome.title: Outcome
outcome.description: ready / awaiting-approval / blocked / exited / changed / timeout / hibernated (the session is hibernated: nothing will happen until it is woken, so the wait returns at once with its kept screen; session.wake or session.input wakes it).

matched.title: Matched
matched.description: True when the outcome is what `until` asked for.

SessionWaitResult.title: SessionWaitResult
SessionWaitResult.description: Why a wait ended, and the screen at that moment.

scopes.title: Scopes
scopes.description: Replace the login's scopes as well.

revoke_sessions.title: Revoke Sessions
revoke_sessions.description: Also revoke every live session this user holds.

id.title: Id
id.description: Session id, in either form: Vogt's `ses_…` id or the engine's session UUID (`engine_session_id` in session.list; the only id an unlinked session has).

role.title: Role
role.description: `oversight` nominates the session to supervise others (and pins it awake); `worker` makes it an ordinary session again and, for a session that was oversight, lifts that pin so the idle policy applies again.

reason.title: Reason
reason.description: Why this write is being made (audited).

policy.title: Policy
policy.description: none: observe and never speak. comment_only: post comments authored here. full: also create, label, and close/reopen. Never deletion, history rewriting or force.

template.title: Template
template.description: Session template to run, by name or by tag — the engine expands it against the deployment's templates. Use this to run an agent rather than a plain shell: `claude` (or `codex`, `opencode`, `klaudia`) starts that agent under the deployment's protected wrapper, so a request to *do* something in a session names one here. Omitted means a plain shell, which does nothing until typed into.

task.title: Task
task.description: What the session's agent should do, in the user's words. Folded into the brief as its Task section; an agent template (Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, Klaudia) is started with a first prompt telling it to read the brief and carry that task out, so 'start a session on X and check its containers' opens an agent already checking them. A plain shell only gets the brief's path in VOGT_ENGINE_AGENT_TASK_PROMPT_FILE, so pair a task with `template` when it is something to carry out. Omitted on an agent start, the task is taken from `reason` (a leading `Task:` dropped); a `review` purpose gets a default review task.

files.title: Files
files.description: Files the task touches, each `path` or `path:start-end`. Rendered under Touch points; a line range is a hint, not a slice of the file.

symbols.title: Symbols
symbols.description: Symbols the task touches. Rendered under Touch points.

done.title: Done
done.description: What finished looks like, one line each. Rendered under Touch points.

gates.title: Gates
gates.description: Checks that must pass before the task is done. Rendered under Touch points.

repo_map.title: Repo Map
repo_map.description: Include a two-level outline of the touch-point directories in the brief. Omitted means include one when touch points name files, and not otherwise. The outline is capped; it is a map, not a listing.

permission_mode.title: Permission Mode
permission_mode.description: The agent's permission posture. `default`: Claude Code's own mode (auto) with the deployment's driven-session policy — routine safe work proceeds, prod-mutating, destructive, shared-resource and secret-exposing actions are denied. `accept_edits`: file edits auto-accepted, everything else asks. `bypass`: no permission checks at all, for one trusted task — only a person may grant it (an agent is refused), and it is audited. Claude Code, Codex, opencode and Klaudia templates. Codex maps the same three postures: `default` is `-a on-request -s danger-full-access`; `accept_edits` adds `approvals_reviewer="auto_review"`; `bypass` is `--dangerously-bypass-approvals-and-sandbox` and stays people-only. A named Codex requirements file that is missing, empty or unreadable refuses the Codex launch (400) and does not fall through to bypass. Klaudia takes `default` and `bypass` only (its `acceptEdits` is an alias for its default autonomous mode, so `accept_edits` is refused).

account.title: Account
account.description: Run the session under a named Claude Code subscription account (a name from the engine's ENGINE_AGENT_CLAUDE_ACCOUNTS). Omitted uses the engine's default account. Claude Code templates only; an unknown name is refused, never started on the default login.

resume.title: Resume
resume.description: Continue a previous conversation of the template's agent CLI instead of starting a new one: its own conversation id, mapped to `claude --resume <id>`, `codex resume <id>`, `opencode --session <id>` or `klaudia --resume <id>`. A Claude Code (or Klaudia) session Vogt started fresh has the engine session id (`engine_session_id`) as its conversation id, so a session lost to a restart can be resumed by that. The engine starts a resumed conversation in the directory its transcript records (when inside the workspace), so one begun under a worktree or a parent folder resumes from any project. Requires `template`; letters, digits and . _ - only, never a leading dash.

name.title: Name
name.description: Session name. Derived from the subject if omitted.

model.title: Model
model.description: Model id for the agent CLI this template runs, e.g. 'gpt-5.6' or 'claude-sonnet-4-5'. Omitted means the CLI's own default. Requires `template`: a plain shell has no model. A template that cannot be told which model to use refuses rather than ignoring this.

effort.title: Effort
effort.description: Reasoning effort for the agent CLI, e.g. 'low' / 'medium' / 'high'. Omitted means the CLI's own default. Requires `template`: a plain shell has no effort to set, so do not volunteer one for a terminal that runs no agent.

autopilot.title: Autopilot
autopilot.description: Keep the agent working unattended: its brief tells it to carry on when its next step needs no person, stopping only when it is blocked on a person (reported with session_report_blocked) or no unblocked work is left (then it prints `AUTOPILOT: DONE`). The engine also re-prompts it whenever it stops at its prompt with work left, and its idle policy leaves it awake. Omitted means on for an agent template started with a `task`, off otherwise; `false` turns it off.

role.title: Role
role.description: `oversight` nominates the session to supervise others (drive rollouts, check on and revive worker sessions): it is pinned awake, so it comes back by itself after a redeploy, and the GUI lists it first. `worker` (default) is every other session. Only a person starts an oversight session; an agent caller is refused. Change it later with session.set_role.

from_handoff.title: From Handoff
from_handoff.description: Start a fresh session from a work item's hand-off comment: the work item ref (e.g. WI-7). Refused when that item has no hand-off comment, and refused when `work_item` is also given and names a different item. The brief carries the latest hand-off.

review_of.title: Review Of
review_of.description: Start a reviewer on this work item (e.g. WI-7) instead of a worker. The brief checks the diff named by the item's latest hand-off against the item's own acceptance criteria, and it does not carry the work on. Refused without a work item — a review is of an item — and when `work_item` or `from_handoff` names a different one.

budget.description: Limits the engine enforces on this session (C7): a soft warning as one is approached, then hibernation (trigger `budget`) when one is reached. Omitted means the default for an agent template started with a `task` as a worker — 120 turns and 90 minutes of wall clock, no context limit — and no budget otherwise. An empty object sets no limits, which is how a start declines the default.

worktree.title: Worktree
worktree.description: Start the session in a git worktree of its own rather than in the project's shared checkout (WI-1298). The engine cuts the worktree from the project's integration branch — `agent_policy.base_branch` when the project states one, otherwise `main` — onto a new branch `<work item>-<session>` (or `<project>-<session>` when no work item is given), and the session's working directory is that worktree. The shared checkout is never written to, so a dirty tree there cannot leak into the session and the session cannot disturb it. Requires a project, or a work item that belongs to one. Unset, the purpose's dispatch profile decides (WI-1323), and with no purpose the session opens in the project's checkout, as `false` does. Cannot be combined with `cwd` (WI-1671). Recorded on the audit row.

cwd.title: Cwd
cwd.description: Open the session in this existing directory instead of the project's registered checkout (WI-1671). Use it when a worktree already exists and `worktree=true` cannot cut a new one — a private origin the engine cannot fetch, for example. The path must exist, must sit under the workspace's `Active/` directory (the parent of the project's checkout), must not be inside that checkout (a subdirectory shares its git toplevel; a linked worktree nested under it does not), and must be a git worktree of the same repository (the same `commondir`). Anything else is refused, and so is combining it with an explicit `worktree=true`. A purpose profile that would have set `worktree` does not, when `cwd` is given. Recorded as the session's cwd.

cold_wake_opt_out.title: Cold Wake Opt Out
cold_wake_opt_out.description: Never compact this session on a cold wake (WI-2037): every wake resumes its full transcript, whatever the deployment's cold_wake_compaction says. Changeable later at session_hibernate.

reason.title: Reason
reason.description: Why this write is being made (audited).

purpose.title: Purpose
purpose.description: What the session is for (WI-1323, design §2.4): implement, implement-careful, review, mechanical, investigate or design. The deployment's dispatch profile for it fills template, model, effort, budget, worktree, repo_map and autopilot wherever this start leaves them unset; a value given here wins and is audited as an override. Recorded on the session.

StartSessionParams.title: StartSessionParams
StartSessionParams.description:
Open a terminal for a work item, or for a project.

At most one of `work_item` and `project`. A session always belongs to a
project — the work item's own, when one is given — because the working
directory comes from the project registry and nowhere else.

** Giving **neither** is allowed only when the deployment has
configured a scratch project, and resolves to it. It exists for the spoken
request with no subject — "research the best risotto in Wollongong" — which
has no work item and no repository but still needs a registered tree to
open in. The scratch project is a project like any other: registered, with
a root path somebody chose. What is *not* allowed is inventing a directory,
which is the failure the registry-owned `cwd` rule exists against.

clone.description: Set when this instance's data was cloned from another instance's backup (`vogt clone`); absent on an instance that never was.

disk.description: The workspace volume, when a session engine answers. needs_attention once used space passes its threshold.

id.title: Id
id.description: Session id, in either form: Vogt's `ses_…` id or the engine's session UUID (`engine_session_id` in session.list; the only id an unlinked session has).

reason.title: Reason
reason.description: Why this write is being made (audited).

pending.title: Pending
pending.description: Migrations this build carries that are not applied yet.

StoreMigration.title: StoreMigration
StoreMigration.description: One store's schema: what is applied against what this build carries.

subject.title: Subject
subject.description: An exact subject key, or a glob pattern when --pattern is set.

project.title: Project
project.description: Limit the suppression to one project.

Suppression.title: Suppression
Suppression.description:
An audited decision that an observed subject is not work.

Lives in the declared store because it is a decision, not an
observation — which is exactly why it survives re-observation of the same
subject, and why a dismissal recorded in the evidence store could never
have worked.

project.title: Project
project.description: Narrow the sweep to one project. Scope is never widened.

collectors.title: Collectors
collectors.description: Collector names; omit to run all of them.

offline_only.title: Offline Only
offline_only.description: Skip every collector that needs the network (NFR-PO2).

disk.description: The workspace volume, when a session engine answers. needs_attention once used space passes its threshold.

Token.title: Token
Token.description:
A scoped credential bound to an actor.

Never carries the secret: only the hash is stored, and the secret is
shown once at issue time. A model that could round-trip the credential
is a model that leaks it into logs and API responses.

ref.title: Ref
ref.description: Work item reference, e.g. WI-7. Alias: `id`.

reason.title: Reason
reason.description: Why the item is moving (audited, required on every write). With `walk`, each hop records this reason annotated with the hop.

walk.title: Walk
walk.description: Walk the shortest path of valid edges to `to_state`, one audited transition per hop (e.g. open -> in_progress -> review -> done). Only the workflow's own edges are taken and finished states are never passed through, so no review step is skipped.

UnpromotedWorkItem.title: UnpromotedWorkItem
UnpromotedWorkItem.description: A work item named by a commit the lane has not deployed.

state.title: State
state.description: `closed` ends it; `initiative publish` then proposes closing its tracking issues.

UpdateInitiativeParams.title: UpdateInitiativeParams
UpdateInitiativeParams.description:
Correct an initiative after creation, or close and reopen it.

The slug is its identity — forge tracking issues carry the
``initiative:<slug>`` label — so a new title leaves the slug as it was.
Every field left unset keeps its current value.

repo_url.title: Repo Url
repo_url.description: Leave unset to keep the current value.

exclusions.title: Exclusions
exclusions.description: Replaces the current list entirely. Leave unset to keep it; pass an empty list to collect everything.

agent_policy.description: Replaces the project's agent policy entirely. Leave unset to keep it. `forbidden_text` entries are regexes and must compile, and so must `landing.branch_pattern` once `{n}` stands for a number; `landing.merge_mode` is `fast_forward` or `rebase` — `merge` is refused. A pattern that does not compile is refused rather than stored.

reason.title: Reason
reason.description: Why this write is being made (audited).

UpdateProjectParams.title: UpdateProjectParams
UpdateProjectParams.description:
Correct a project's declaration after registration.

Deliberately narrow. `lifecycle_state` is absent because it has its own
operation with a validated edge (`project transition`), and the observed
fields are absent because nothing declares them. What is left is what a
registration can get wrong and nothing else could fix — where the project
is published, what collection should skip — and the agent policy, which is
data the project states rather than something derived.

limited.title: Limited
limited.description: A window at 100% or a hit not yet reset.

tokens_5h.title: Tokens 5H

WatchTriggerModel.title: WatchTriggerModel
WatchTriggerModel.description:
What a watch waits for (WI-2036). `kind` picks the fields that apply:

- `pr`: `project` + `number`; fires when the PR reads one of `on`
  (default merged or closed).
- `ci`: `project` + `sha` or `pr`; fires when every run on that revision
  (a PR's head) — each named required check in `checks` (at least
  one) — has been observed and concluded.
- `work_item`: `work_item`; fires when it is in one of `states` (default
  a terminal state).
- `session`: `session`; fires when it ends (`until=ended`: exited,
  hibernated or stopped) or also when it declares itself done
  (`until=done`).

Forge triggers read what the collectors observed, so they fire within a
sweep interval of the event; Vogt triggers within the watch interval.

WorkItemBranchView.title: WorkItemBranchView
WorkItemBranchView.description:
One branch bound to a work item, declared or observed or both.

 `source` is the whole point: `declared` is a branch a Vogt-started session
 said it would use, `observed` is one a sweep actually found in the
 checkout, and `both` is the two agreeing. A branch that is one but not the
 other is drift — declared and observed are kept separate and never merged
, so the surface can show the disagreement rather than paper over
 it. `last_commit_age_seconds` is derived from `last_commit_at` at read time
 so it is always current without the observation churning every sweep.

WorkItemGitStory.title: WorkItemGitStory
WorkItemGitStory.description:
Where a work item is in git, derived from branches + the PR edge.

 A single read-only answer to "where is this in git?", assembled from the
 already-observed branch bindings and the `implemented_by` PR edge
. `phase` is a derived opinion shown *beside* the workflow state, not
 written onto it: a `merged` phase on an item still `in_progress` is exactly
 the disagreement this is meant to make visible. `drift` carries the obvious
 contradictions. `task_conclusion_available` records that the task-run
 conclusion is an engine-side seam not yet folded in, so the phase is honest
 about what it is *not* considering.

WorkItemPullRequestView.title: WorkItemPullRequestView
WorkItemPullRequestView.description:
The pull request observed to implement a work item.

Read from the `forge.pull_request` observation the `implemented_by` edge
points at — never declared. `state` is the *derived* PR state, richer than
the observation's raw open/closed/merged: `draft` and `in-review` are read
off the PR's own draft flag and review decision so the git phase can tell
"opened" from "being reviewed". Every field carries where it came from and
how old it is, so the surface can say "observed 4 min ago from GitHub"
rather than presenting a stale rollup as current.
